subtopics.title: Three Methods, One Shelf of Stock

questions.question: Under the periodic inventory system, cost of sales is computed as:
options: Opening stock plus purchases less closing stock, after a physical count
A running total updated with every sale
Sales less gross profit percentage, always
Closing stock less opening stock

questions.question: Specific identification is appropriate for:
options: Identical boxes of tea
Vehicles identified by chassis number, jewellery and machinery — few, expensive, distinguishable items
Juice boxes in a fridge
Any stock in a periodic system

questions.question: FIFO is best described as:
options: A claim about which physical box left the shelf first
A method valuing all units at one pooled price
An assumption for valuation that the oldest COSTS are charged out first, leaving the newest costs in stock
A rule requiring stock to be sold before it expires

questions.question: The GAAP principle of consistency requires that:
options: Stock always be valued at selling price
Every business use FIFO
Profits be smoothed between years
A chosen valuation method be kept year after year, with any change justified and disclosed

questions.question: Radebe Electrical has 300 units left after deliveries of 150 at R50 (November) and 350 at R48 (August). FIFO closing stock is:
options: R14 700 — 150 units at R50 plus 150 units at R48
R12 600 — 300 units at R42
R15 000 — 300 units at R50

questions.question: With stock available costing R57 300 and FIFO closing stock of R14 700, cost of sales is:
options: R42 600 — the cost of everything available less what remains

questions.question: In a year of rising prices, FIFO produces:
options: Low closing stock and low gross profit
High closing stock and low gross profit
High closing stock and high gross profit — the cheapest old costs go to cost of sales
The same profit as weighted average

questions.question: The classic FIFO error is:
options: Valuing closing stock at selling price
Adding carriage to the cost of stock
Subtracting closing stock from sales
Building the remaining units forward from opening stock instead of backwards from the newest deliveries

subtopics.title: Weighted Average Worked to the Rand

questions.question: Stock available cost R57 300 for 1 250 units. The weighted average cost per unit is:
options: R46,25 — the average of the four prices

questions.question: The self-check for weighted average figures is that closing stock plus cost of sales must equal:
options: Sales for the year
The full cost of stock available — R13 752 plus R43 548 rebuilds R57 300
Gross profit
Opening stock

questions.question: FIFO gross profit exceeds weighted average gross profit by R948 — exactly the difference in the two closing stock values — because:
options: FIFO records more sales
Weighted average ignores opening stock
Whatever value stays in closing stock has by that amount been kept out of cost of sales
It is a coincidence of these numbers

questions.question: Averaging the four purchase PRICES of R42, R45, R48 and R50 instead of weighting by units is wrong because:
options: Prices may not be added together
It always understates stock value
The result must be rounded to the nearest rand
It ignores how many units arrived at each price — 500 units at R45 must count more than 150 at R50

subtopics.title: Validation, Ethics and Control of Stock

questions.question: Records show 300 fans but the count finds 275, with weighted average cost R45,84. The trading stock deficit is:
options: R1 146 — twenty-five missing units at R45,84, written off as an expense
R1 750 — twenty-five units at selling price
R1 146 added to closing stock

questions.question: The buyer, receiver, recorder and counter of stock should be different people because:
options: It creates more jobs
One person doing all four can invent deliveries and hide theft indefinitely
The law forbids overtime
Counting is a specialist skill

questions.question: Overstating closing stock inflates profit, which could deceive:
options: Only the storeman
Nobody, since stock and profit are unrelated
Lenders, shareholders and bonus schemes — all reading a profit built on fiction
Only SARS, which then collects too little tax

questions.question: Switching valuation method in a convenient year is described as the polite version of manipulation because:
options: Methods may never legally change
It requires no arithmetic
Auditors never examine methods
It shifts profit between years without any lie about quantities — which is exactly why consistency is a GAAP principle and changes must be disclosed

subtopics.title: The Fridge That Ate the Profits

questions.question: Karabo's fridge becomes a philosophy problem when the wholesaler's price rises because:
options: Identical boxes bought at R8 and R10 carry no receipts saying which is which
Cold juice loses value
She forgot how many boxes she bought
The fridge broke down

questions.question: Specific identification works for Karabo's yoghurt tubs but not her juice boxes because:
options: Yoghurt is more expensive than juice
The tubs are few and distinguishable by their dated labels; thirty-five identical boxes are not
Juice boxes may not be individually valued by law
Yoghurt never changes price

questions.question: The value placed on the 35 boxes matters because:
options: It sets next season's selling price
The wholesaler demands it
Boxes in the fridge are cost not yet used up — the fridge's value and the profit line share one pot of rands
It determines the electricity bill

questions.question: Valuing the fridge HIGH means this year's profit:
options: Falls by the same amount
Is unaffected
Doubles
Rises with it — less cost has been charged against sales

subtopics.title: Two Honest Answers to One Question

questions.question: Karabo bought 45 boxes at R8 and 30 at R10, and 35 remain. First-in-first-out values the fridge at:
options: R340 — all 30 of the R10 boxes plus 5 of the R8 boxes
R350 — 35 boxes at R10

questions.question: The weighted average value of the fridge is R308 because:
options: R10 minus R8 is R2
R660 across 75 boxes is R8,80 a box, and 35 boxes remain
Half the boxes are new
R560 less R208 is R308

questions.question: The two methods give profits of R240 and R208. The R32 difference is explained by:
options: An arithmetic error in one method
Different sales figures
The R32 difference between the two fridge values — whatever the fridge holds, the profit line released
The cost of electricity

questions.question: Across the years, the choice of method:
options: Creates extra profit under FIFO
Destroys profit under weighted average
Changes the total cost of the boxes
Neither creates nor destroys a rand — every box's cost is charged eventually; the method only decides which year carries it

subtopics.title: When the Count and the Book Disagree

questions.question: The notebook says 35 boxes, the fridge holds 32, and boxes cost R8,80. The deficit written off is about:
options: R26 — three missing boxes at cost
R42 — three boxes at selling price
Nothing, until the thief is found

questions.question: Three boxes a week is worth taking seriously because:
options: Juice expires quickly
That is more than 150 boxes a year — weeks of profit gone to a ghost
The wholesaler counts boxes on delivery
The fridge holds only 35 boxes

questions.question: Stock counts are most reliable when done by:
options: The storeman who keeps the stock, on a fixed schedule
The buyer who ordered the stock
Someone other than the stock's keeper, on unannounced days
The supplier's delivery driver

questions.question: Puffing stock UP and squashing it DOWN are both lies in rands; the second one specifically:
options: Impresses the bank
Raises the share price
Earns managers bigger bonuses
Shrinks reported profit and with it the tax owed to SARS
